title: I2S (Inter-IC Sound) audio interface
summary: I2S is a serial bus for digital audio. Signals: SCK (serial clock), WS (word select / LRCLK, 0=left, 1=right), SD (serial data). Data is transmitted MSB-first, synchronized to SCK. The WS frequency = sample rate (e.g., 44.1 kHz for CD audio). SCK frequency = sample rate * bits per sample * 2 (stereo). Common: 44.1/48/96/192 kHz, 16/24/32 bits.

structure.meaning: Serial clock (bit clock). Frequency = sample_rate * bits_per_sample * 2 (stereo).
Word select (left/right clock). Frequency = sample rate. 0 = left channel, 1 = right channel.
Serial data, MSB-first, 2's complement. One data line per channel (or TDM for multi-channel).
Master clock (256x or 384x sample rate). Used by DAC/ADC for internal clocking.
Left-justified, right-justified (I2S standard), or TDM (time-division multiplexed for multi-channel).

notes: I2S is the standard interface between audio codecs and microcontrollers/SoCs.
TDM (Time Division Multiplexing) extends I2S to 8+ channels on a single data line.
I2S is used in audio DACs, ADCs, and digital microphones.
PCM (Pulse Code Modulation) is the underlying data format for I2S.
